headline: High: n8n’s server-side workflow execution can overwrite shared files and invoke external integrations, creating dangerous pairwise leakage and cascading-error paths with pathway.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read/write the server filesystem and orchestrate AI Agent sub-nodes, so if pathway outputs are routed into n8n workflows, file content can become instruction-like input. Pathway itself has no shared channel or parser surface documented, so the risk is inferred from n8n’s workflow plumbing rather than direct interaction evidence.
conditions: IF pathway output is written into a file that n8n later ingests as workflow input
IF n8n AI Agent nodes treat pathway-produced text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every pathway output before n8n consumes it
Route pathway outputs through a strict JSON schema validator
Disable any n8n step that interprets file text as instructions
Use separate directories for pathway outputs and n8n inputs
requires-engineering: add content-signing or provenance metadata end-to-end

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n has broad network egress and server filesystem access, while pathway is a document-processing agent with no network egress and no filesystem access. If they share a workspace or n8n reads sensitive documents that pathway processes, n8n can transmit those contents to third-party integrations. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents access the same document set or shared workspace
IF n8n workflow nodes send those documents to external APIs or SaaS integrations
mitigations: Restrict n8n credentials to least-privilege scopes
Separate sensitive documents into a pathway-only workspace
Disable external integrations for workflows handling sensitive data
Turn off file-content forwarding in n8n steps
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before any outbound node

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n can write the server filesystem and execute shell commands; pathway is a document-processing system with no write or shell capability. If both operate on the same shared directory or connected systems, n8n’s writes can race with pathway’s reads or downstream processing, and the rubric treats shared mutable resources with unrestricted writes as dangerous. Pathway’s lack of write capability does not remove the conflict because n8n alone can corrupt shared state.
conditions: IF n8n and pathway target the same filesystem path or connected mutable resource
IF n8n workflows run concurrently with pathway jobs without locking
mitigations: Put n8n and pathway on separate directories
Add file locks around shared outputs
Disable n8n shell steps for shared resources
Serialize jobs that touch the same dataset
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination or a queue

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n’s AI Agent node can orchestrate tools and downstream integrations, so if pathway outputs are fed into n8n without verification, n8n may act on incorrect or malformed document-processing results. Pathway does not provide a documented verification layer here, so the cascade is inferred from n8n’s action-taking role and the absence of a checked handoff.
conditions: IF pathway output is used as authoritative input to an n8n workflow
IF n8n triggers emails, API calls, or database updates from that output without validation
mitigations: Insert a human review step before n8n actions
Validate pathway output against a schema
Require confidence thresholds before downstream actions
Log and diff pathway outputs before execution
requires-engineering: add automated cross-checking against source documents

E_compliance.rationale: n8n handles per-credential secrets and broad integrations, while pathway is unverified and has no stated residency or retention controls. The only concrete compliance concern visible is that n8n may process whatever the workflow processes, so if regulated data is routed through it, policy mismatch is possible. Pathway’s lack of documented controls limits certainty, so this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through n8n workflows
IF n8n retention or logging exceeds the policy required for that data class
mitigations: Review n8n retention settings
Avoid sending regulated data to unverified workflows
Mask secrets before workflow ingestion
Document data-class handling for each integration
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement
